A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LayerCraft framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original LayerCraft benchmark results and CoT ablations in Tables 1–2, alongside generated images, editing demonstrations, and OIN analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds GenEval results, a human evaluation, and quantitative MagicBrush editing results in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: The coordinator, ChainArchitect planning procedure, dual-LoRA OIN, attention mixing, and iterative bounding-box refinement remain unchanged. The additional evaluations do not introduce a method component or procedural modification.

E1.justification: v3 substantially expands documented evaluation coverage with GenEval compositional prompts and MagicBrush ground-truth multi-turn editing data. v2 mentions forthcoming GenEval results but supplies none. IPA300K training, T2I-CompBench evaluation, and existing qualitative editing scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The new MagicBrush comparison in Table 5 introduces HIVE, InstructPix2Pix, and the MagicBrush method alongside GenArtist, substantially extending comparisons to dedicated editing competitors. Existing T2I-CompBench and subject-driven inpainting comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a study with 30 participants rating five systems on 15 challenging prompts using four five-point criteria. It also evaluates one-fifth of MagicBrush with L1/L2, CLIP-I, DINO, and CLIP-T metrics. These are new evaluation designs; previously reported training and ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The CoT-component ablations in Table 2, attention-mixing alternatives and failures in Section 10.1, bounding-box refinement example, and qualitative editing case studies retain the same evidence. No new ablation, robustness test, or error analysis is added.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports means and standard deviations of human ratings. The existing four dataset-generation seeds remain unchanged; no increase in repeated model runs, confidence intervals, or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 add substantial results: LayerCraft ties GPT-4o at 0.84 overall on GenEval and 4.2 for overall human ratings. The new MagicBrush comparison reports CLIP-I 0.9121 versus GenArtist's 0.9071, alongside slightly worse L1/L2 distances. All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 and existing qualitative examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The object-list formulation, dual attention equations, and masked output combination in Section 3 remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and v3 introduces no new formal definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: CoT-guided structured generation, coordinated agents, and consistent layered object editing. Their claims about avoiding model retraining also remain unchanged. Added evaluations support existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 9.2 adds an interpretation of MagicBrush results that prioritizes semantic alignment over pixelwise distances, acknowledging GenArtist's better L1/L2 scores. It also interprets human ratings as supporting prompt fidelity and naturalness. Existing computational-overhead limitations and mechanism explanations are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation and access disclosures remain unchanged, including GPT-4o temperature 0.1, rank-4 LoRAs, OIN training for 20,000 iterations on 50K IPA300K pairs, hardware, and dataset preparation. Both versions still describe code and dataset releases as forthcoming.

R1.justification: v3 retains all 54 references and adds six: GenEval, MagicBrush, SmartAvatar, Agentic 3D Scene Generation, ChatCam, and WorldCraft. These extend benchmark attribution and agent-related citations without substantially revising novelty claims or positioning against existing approaches.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 4.3 and appendix Sections 9.1–9.2, while retaining nearly all existing prose and section order. Author emails are removed, and an exchange-student footnote and NeurIPS 2025 designation are added. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 3–5, places Table 1 alongside Table 2, and reflows the title page and several appendix figures. All 15 existing figures retain identical image content; the original tables retain their structure and values.

improvement.justification: Tables 3–5 strengthen empirical support, particularly by adding quantitative multi-turn editing evidence where v2 relied on qualitative demonstrations. The gain is limited by sparse evaluation details and overstated summaries: overall GenEval and human-quality scores tie GPT-4o, while small rating differences receive no significance analysis. The added evidence improves assessability without establishing the broad superiority suggested by some new prose.
